content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I have several [article_no] modules in operation and recently got a new [article_no] for an upcoming project. To test, I updated and downloaded my existing program, modifying the 'hardware' to the new version. My setup uses all four analog inputs, so I enabled them via Hardware I/O settings ('enable 4 AIs'). I connected analog DC voltages (2–5 V) expecting the program to react, but nothing happened. Then I created a simple test program where all analog inputs go through amplifiers to markers, with 0-10V signal and adjustable gain. Displaying the amplifier values showed no signal. Checking the internal menu for 'AI' values and the online monitor also showed all inputs at zero. When I connected a 10V digital signal to each input and checked the digital display, the inputs registered correctly. My digital input program activated relays as expected, verifying this function works. It appears the new module is not responding to analog signals, only digital. If anyone has advice, I'd appreciate it. Regards,

When testing with external voltage sources, make sure to connect the 0V terminals of those sources to the 0V terminal of the module's power supply. To check if analog inputs are working, you can apply the positive side of a 24V supply to I7 and observe AI1 in the menu; it should display a value of 1000 units.

Thanks for your suggestion regarding the ground connection. I realized my power inputs are labeled P1 and P2, not L1 and M, which seemed odd. Unfortunately, I've ordered the wrong module version! I have several DC modules ([article_no]), but now I have an AC/DC version, which does not support analog inputs, only digital. Is anyone interested in exchanging this new AC/DC module for a DC module with relay outputs? Regards, [user_name] PS. Requesting the older version as a replacement is intentional since I need compatibility with a legacy module.

I'm facing a similar issue. I'm running +24VDC through an 8.2k resistor and a 470-ohm resistor to 0V from I8. The input is detected on the digital screen, but the analog input (AI2/I8) does not respond to voltage changes. It seems like the threshold trigger block isn't functioning. Measurements show 1.2 VDC with the resistor configuration and 23.5 VDC when shorted, but the Ax value doesn't change. The same trigger block works fine in previous module versions. I find the threshold trigger screen confusing and want the output to activate above a certain voltage, acting like a normally closed digital input so the input turns off if the device is removed or damaged, ideally without adding more components.
Can you share your module's order number?
This module does not include analog inputs. Only modules running exclusively on pure DC supply voltage offer analog inputs (0–10V).
Wow, I hadn’t noticed I had the wrong version. My apologies, and thanks for clarifying!
If a basic module includes analog inputs, it will be indicated on the hardware itself. Attached is an image of [article_no] for reference.
I neglected to check the part number and assumed I had the correct module—problem solved, thanks for the help!

Hello all, I’d like to share my experience with a similar issue. While setting up the analog input (0–10V) on my module, I initially tried to use the wrong analog channels in ladder logic, but switching to the correct analog input channels resolved the issue. Hope this helps!
Welcome to the forum. That’s not a new problem.

analysis.insight_summary: Users encountered nonfunctional analog input channels using their modules and discovered only digital inputs worked. The root cause was ordering an AC/DC version that lacks analog input support, unlike the DC-only models users were accustomed to. This led to confusion and troubleshooting, until users realized the importance of verifying the module version and specifications before deployment.
analysis.user_expectations: Users anticipated that the new module would support analog input channels similarly to previous DC-only models, enabling program control via analog voltage inputs and compatibility with logic blocks requiring analog values.
